conviction_note: This is a pre-released print: the 9 September RNS gave H1 adjusted PBT (~£14.8m) and reset FY26 to ~£38.0m, and the 23 July RNS had already given revenue, completions and adviser numbers, so there is almost no P&L information left to discover and print_vs_bar is ~0 by construction. What is left is the dividend line (formulaic, and the formula says up, not cut), the tone on the £38m, and a stock 8.2% off a 52-week low with a 2.05% disclosed short building into it; my findings net to +1.4 and I carry +2.0 because this name's own Interim Results reactions are +13.24% (2024-09-24) and +7.94% (2025-09-23) and the UK tail is not truncated, while holding well under the 4.83% move proxy precisely because the numbers are already out.

findings.finding: The interim dividend is set by formula at one third of ~50% of expected full-year adjusted post-tax profit, and FY26 guidance of ~£38.0m is still ~5% profit growth on 2025 — so the arithmetic points to an interim DPS of roughly 7.5-7.8p against 7.2p last year, an increase, at a moment when the default retail read after a 20% profit warning is a cut.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The last time MAB moved this line it was the February 2025 policy reset that took FY DPS from 28.2p to 22.5p — a cut of ~20% — and the stock still rose 8.12% on the 2026-03-17 Final Results that confirmed it and promised a progressive policy. The line has not been a source of downside on this name; the two prior Interim Results prints that carried a dividend declaration moved +13.24% and +7.94%.
findings.original_quote: As previously announced, the Board is pleased to confirm payment of an ordinary dividend equivalent to of 50% of adjusted post-tax profit. This equates to a full-year dividend of 22.5p per share (2024: 28.2p), of which 7.2p was paid at the interim stage. ... As previously indicated, the Board intends to adopt a progressive dividend policy going forward.
findings.why_not_priced: If it were priced the stock would not be trading at 382.5p against an implied ~23p full-year DPS — a 6.1% yield on a business with 0.1x leverage, £3.3m net debt, 121% adjusted cash conversion and £56.7m of regulatory-capital headroom. Three analysts cover the name (baseline consensus.analyst_count = 3) and the two sell-side aggregators reachable here still carry price targets of 975p-1250p against a 382.5p spot, i.e. nobody has republished a post-warning model in public. The marginal holder of a £222m Main Market name with three analysts is domestic retail and adviser money that reads the dividend line first, and the run-up (-26.16% over 20 days) is the shape of a market that has priced a cut, not an increase.
findings.independence: Corroborated by a different document: the 2025 interims set the precedent that the interim payment is one third of the expected full-year dividend (7.2p of 22.5p) and describe it as 'in line with the new capital allocation framework and dividend policy announced in February 2025' — https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/mortgage-advice-bureau-holdings---mab1/interim-results/9124509 (2025-09-23). The £38.0m FY guidance that drives the arithmetic comes from the 2026-09-09 RNS, which is also the document behind findings 2 and 3.

findings.finding: Everything in tomorrow's P&L has already been released: the 23 July RNS gave H1 revenue (~£160m, +8%), completions (£16.5bn, +16%), mainstream advisers (2,194) and revenue per adviser (£74k), and the 9 September RNS gave H1 adjusted PBT (~£14.8m) after the period-end reporting process had completed — and the incoming CFO does not take office until 1 October, so the rebasing risk that usually accompanies a management change sits after this print, not at it.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: MAB's price-sensitive news lands on trading updates, not on the scheduled release: the two largest moves in the 15-event observed record are a Trading Update (+14.92%, 2025-01-23) and a Trading Update (-20.08%, 2026-09-09), while the AGM statements that merely confirmed a known position moved +0.24% and -2.04%.
findings.original_quote: Adjusted profit before tax is expected to be approximately £14.6m, in line with the equivalent period last year (H1 2025: £14.5m). The number of mainstream advisers at 30 June 2026 was up 3% on the prior year end to 2,194 (31 December 2025: 2,135).
findings.why_not_priced: The pre-release itself is wire copy and is priced. What is not priced is the consequence for the DISTRIBUTION of tomorrow's move: the baseline's move proxy of 4.83% and the 4.09% historical median are computed on prints that carried unknown numbers, and a market that had correctly collapsed its expected move would not have left the stock at a 76.7% 20-day realised vol with 1.1m shares crossing on 18 September. If this were priced the option-equivalent would be flat and it is the historic reaction scale that is still being applied. The CFO-handover timing is the part nobody has written down: the outgoing CFO signs this statement and the successor presents on 25 September, three days after the window closes.
findings.independence: The CFO dates come from a separate RNS — Group CFO Designate appointed 29 June 2026, Emilie McCarthy departing 30 September, Jo Stent effective 1 October: https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/mortgage-advice-bureau-holdings---mab1/appointment-of-group-cfo-designate-board-changes/9641666 . SHARED DOCUMENT WARNING: the £14.8m half of this finding rests on the same 2026-09-09 RNS as finding 3, which points the other way; their net contribution from that document is -0.2 points and both are sized as halves of one read, not as two independent facts.

findings.finding: The £38.0m full-year guide implies £23.2m of adjusted PBT in H2 — 61% of the year and +57% on H1 — against £21.8m in H2 2025, and it was set by a board that told the market on 23 July that it expected 'full-year results to be in line with expectations' and that the CEO 'remain[ed] confident in the Group's outlook for the full year', then cut the year by 12.4% forty-seven days later.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The guidance line is where this stock's damage has come from: -20.08% on 2026-09-09 when the FY was cut and -2.96% on 2026-07-23 when it was reiterated with a margin warning. The market has stopped paying for reassurance on this line — the 2026-05-20 AGM statement reiterating 'in line' moved -2.04%.
findings.original_quote: Taking these factors into account, the Group now expects Adjusted profit before tax for the year ending 31 December 2026 of approximately £38.0m. This compares with current market consensus of £43.4m. ... The Group does not expect a meaningful recovery in purchase activity in the short term.
findings.why_not_priced: The £38m headline is priced; the residual arithmetic behind it is not, because no one has published it — three analysts cover the name and no post-warning note text is public. If the market had done the subtraction, the 8.2% bounce off the 15 September low would not have happened into a print whose main job is to defend the most H2-weighted year MAB has ever guided to, in a market where mortgage approvals for house purchase were -15% year-on-year in July and the Bank of England held at 3.75% on 17 September rather than cutting. This is why my emitted number is below the sum of the positive findings alone.
findings.independence: The H2 skew was pre-flagged in a different document — the 23 July RNS: 'profitability in 2026 is expected to be more heavily weighted towards H2 than in prior years' — https://www.tradingview.com/news/reuters.com,2026-07-23:newsml_RSW4750Na:0-reg-mortgage-adv-bureau-trading-update/ . SHARED DOCUMENT WARNING: rests on the same 2026-09-09 RNS as finding 2; see that note.

findings.finding: The Fluent shortfall is an IAS 36 impairment trigger sitting on a balance sheet with £69.7m of goodwill and £53.9m of other intangibles, and MAB's own accounting policy tests goodwill 'whenever events or changes in circumstances indicate that their carrying amount may not be recoverable' — so a statutory charge at the half year is live even though management has framed the shortfall as a timing delay 'pushed into 2027'.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: MAB's statutory line already runs far below its adjusted one and the market has looked through it: FY25 statutory PBT £22.1m against £36.3m adjusted, and basic EPS fell 5.8% while adjusted diluted EPS rose 13.5% — and the stock rose 8.12% on that print (2026-03-17). So the line has a demonstrated history of being ignored by the holders, which is why this is sized at well under half of the dividend finding.
findings.original_quote: Impairment tests on goodwill and other intangible assets with indefinite useful economic lives are undertaken annually at the financial year end or whenever events or changes in circumstances indicate that their carrying amount may not be recoverable. ... Goodwill 69,742 ... Other intangible assets 53,869
findings.why_not_priced: None of the coverage of the 9 September warning — wire, aggregator or the two UK trade titles that carried it — mentions the carrying value of Fluent at all; all of it is written in adjusted-PBT terms. If the market had priced an impairment the de-rate would not have stopped at roughly the capitalised value of the £5m profit deferral. Against it: the charge would be excluded from adjusted PBT by MAB's own definition, the full goodwill test is a year-end exercise, and the outgoing CFO signs this statement — which is why the central size is small and the band is one-sided.
findings.independence: The trigger itself is a different document: 'Fluent's expected contribution to Group Adjusted profit before tax for 2026 is approximately £5m lower than previously anticipated' — https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/mortgage-advice-bureau-holdings---mab1/trading-update-and-revised-2026-expectations/9761840 (2026-09-09).

lessons_applied: 'Positioning is the thing to beat, not the thing to agree with' — the positioning finding restates the same 2.05%/+0.45pp that the baseline already pays +1.23 and -0.90 for in lean_components, so it was cut from +0.9 to +0.5 and the overlap is declared in its independence field rather than left implicit.

'Coverage tells you which regime you are in ... at 3-7 nobody is positioned for a confirmed fact' — the dividend finding is exactly a pre-determined fact on a 3-analyst name, so it went from +1.5 to +1.8.

'A German ad-hoc filed before the print may have pre-released the number ... the UK's is an RNS trading update' — this is the whole shape of the event and it is why expected_move is held to +2.0 against a 4.83% proxy rather than sized off the historical reaction alone.

'Two findings resting on one document are one finding' — findings 2 and 3 both rest on the 2026-09-09 RNS and point opposite ways; both now carry an explicit SHARED DOCUMENT warning and are sized as halves of one read, net -0.2 from that document.

'Keep findings inside the exit window' — moved the Investor Meet Company presentation (25 September), the 1 October CFO handover and the Ben Thompson departure into outside_window, and re-anchored the guidance finding on tomorrow's tone rather than on the H2 outturn.

'Understatement is the hunters' systematic error. Size on the name's own reaction distribution' — this is the one rule pulling the other way and it is why expected_move (+2.0) sits above the finding sum (+1.4): the two observed Interim Results reactions on this name are +13.24% and +7.94% and the UK tail is not truncated.
Net: impact sum +1.5 -> +1.4, expected move unchanged at +2.0, print_vs_bar unchanged at +0.5, findings count unchanged at 5.
